meta.title: Ember — OpenTelemetry for Coding Agents — Crucible
meta.description: Ember is a Go OpenTelemetry Collector distribution that reconstructs agent session trees and groups cross-harness work with ember.work.id. In development.

hero.headline: Session trees. Connected agent work.
hero.subheadline: Ember reconstructs session and workstream trees across processes and machines. It groups related work across coding harnesses with ember.work.id and exports standard OTLP to your existing backend. Content capture is off by default.

problem.heading: Agent telemetry loses the session tree

items.title: Disconnected sessions
items.description: Orchestrators, agents, and subagents run in separate processes and export separate traces. Parent and child relationships disappear.

items.title: Missing work and usage context
items.description: Tokens, credits, cost, MCP calls, and human attribution sit in different harness records. Cross-harness work has no shared identifier.

items.title: Content should stay optional
items.description: Telemetry needs metadata without prompts, tool inputs, or response bodies. Ember uses an explicit allowlist and disables content capture by default.

architecture.heading: A collector for coding harnesses
architecture.diagramAlt: Ember architecture — machine agents and an optional gateway export OTLP to an existing backend
architecture.caption: Ember runs as an agent on each machine. An optional gateway merges machines. Your backend receives standard OTLP.

sessionTree.heading: One session. One trace tree.
sessionTree.description: Ember reconstructs parent and child relationships within each session or workstream. ember.work.id groups related work across harnesses without changing trace IDs or merging every session into a universal trace.
sessionTree.diagramAlt: Ember session tree — orchestrator, agents, subagents, and tool calls reconstructed into one trace tree per session or workstream

loop.heading: Shared context. Connected telemetry.
loop.description: Forge distributes skills, rules, and workflows. Ember traces the work agents do. They integrate through files and open protocols while your harnesses and observability backend stay in place.

value.heading: The context needed to inspect agent work

items.title: Session lineage
items.description: Follow work from orchestrator to agent, subagent, and tool call. Deterministic IDs reconnect records exported by different processes and machines.

items.title: Usage and attribution
items.description: Add tokens, Droid credits, Claude Code cost, MCP server and tool names, and human attribution. Group cross-harness work with ember.work.id.

items.title: Privacy controls
items.description: Export metadata by default. Attribute allowlists decide what leaves each machine, and deny rules take precedence.

otel.heading: Standard OTLP. Your existing backend.
otel.description: Ember is a custom OpenTelemetry Collector distribution written in Go. Harness adapters combine native telemetry with local session records. Upstream collector components provide batching, retries, memory limits, and exporters.

claudeCode.title: Session trees
claudeCode.description: Connect every session, subagent, and tool call with deterministic trace and span IDs. Droid and Claude Code are the initial adapters.

ember.title: Work and usage context
ember.description: Enrich telemetry with ember.work.id, harness and workstream IDs, token and credit metrics, MCP details, and human attribution.

combined.title: Open export
combined.description: Send traces, logs, and metrics over standard OTLP. Keep using Grafana, Datadog, Dash0, or another compatible backend.

otel.footer: These capabilities describe the Ember v1 design. Ember is in development and is not yet released.

dashboard.heading: Planned Grafana dashboards

skills.title: TOOL AND MCP CALLS — LAST 7 DAYS

tokens.title: TOKEN USAGE BY MODEL
tokens.estimatedCost: Native cost metrics stay in the harness's reported currency.

dashboard.caption: Mock data. The v1 design includes Agent tree, Overview, Tools and MCP, and Cost dashboards. Ember is in development.

landscape.heading: Complement the tools you already run
landscape.footer: Ember complements harness telemetry and observability backends. It does not replace either.

items.relationship: Ember adds cross-process session trees and standard OTLP export for Droid work.
Ember keeps native telemetry and fills session-tree, MCP, work, and attribution gaps.
Send Ember's traces, logs, and metrics to an existing OTLP intake.
The v1 design includes dashboards for agent trees, usage, tools and MCP, and cost.
